audit.method: Read from the full term sheet by one AI reviewer, then checked against it twice by independent AI reviewers: first every line of the record against the document, then the document section by section against the record. Not signed off by a person. Every quote is looked up in the PDF text each time the tool runs.
audit.open_points:
Final record: C:\Users\AFarid\Documents\Hackathon\key_credit_terms\data\audited\honeywell_5yr.json. Checker: structure OK; 61 quotes exact, 0 loose, 0 on another page, 0 missing. A diff against the first-audit record shows only the two mandatory_prepayment changes; the other 33 fields and the doc block are identical.

Walking the 12 pages (text dump, plus page images 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 10 and 12) found no term missing from a row that fits it, no content in the wrong row, and no figure taken from the wrong place. The layout is label / value throughout, with no existing / proposed columns. Every amount, percentage and period in the record matches the page it cites.

First auditor's doubts, resolved:
1. doc.date stays empty. No date is printed; the footer "2026 Honeywell Term Sheet" is a label, and kct\llm.py asks for the date "as printed, \"\" if not printed".
2. The four financial covenant rows stay by_reference. The covenant list is open ("including, but not limited to") and defers to the Existing 5-Year Agreement, which is the style guide's open-list case. A search of the dump for ratio, leverage, EBITDA, coverage and net worth finds nothing.
3. info_annual_obligor stays not_stated. The term sheet never mentions obligor accounts, and the field guidance prescribes this wording and status. The open-list rule would also allow by_reference; that is a conflict inside the brief, not something the document can settle.
4. "Lender put" stays, with the printed caveat. Page 2 gives each Lender only a right to terminate its commitment.
5. other_covenants stays by_reference: every listed covenant is "certain ..." with its detail left to the Existing 5-Year Agreement.
6-8. The format departures, the ten lines of 254-362 characters (limit 420) and the three-quote evidence limits are left as they are. Merging or trimming would drop content or exceed the hard limit.
10. Voluntary commitment cancellation, Majority Lenders, the 100 basis point default margin and the page 12 pricing grid have no template row and are not recorded.

What the document itself cannot resolve:
- "Spin Off" is never defined, so the trigger for the $3.0bn reduction and the $3.5bn cap is unknown.
- The Change of Control clause is silent on repayment of a terminating Lender's Advances.
- The board-change exception reads "individuals replaced ... are elected"; the record reads this as the replacement directors.
- Whether the final documents carry a financial covenant, the reporting deadlines, and all covenant baskets depend on the Existing 5-Year Agreement, which was not consulted.

doc.title: Honeywell International Inc. - Summary of Terms and Conditions - $4,000,000,000 5-Year Multi-Currency Revolving Credit Facility
doc.notes: Indicative, undated summary of terms (footer '2026 Honeywell Term Sheet') for a new $4.0bn 5-year unsecured multi-currency revolving credit facility for Honeywell International Inc., delivered to prospective lenders. Terms are on pages 1-11 in a label / value layout; page 12 is the ratings-based 5-Year Pricing Grid. It is not an amendment showing existing and proposed terms: it is a new facility, and payment of accrued amounts and termination of commitments under the Existing 5-Year Agreement dated as of 18 March 2024 is a condition precedent to closing. Representations, covenants and events of default are open lists ('including, but not limited to') to be similar to, and no less favourable to the Company than, that agreement, so most covenant detail is by reference; 'Spin Off' and 'Designated Subsidiaries' are used without definition, 'Eligible Assignees' and 'Rating Condition' are defined only by reference to that agreement, and a 364-Day Facility is mentioned but not described.
